docs.title: AI Audience Builder ⚡
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for the AI Audience Builder, a high-performance, principal-grade platform for AI-driven advertising segmentation.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Links
docs.text:
• Getting Started: Get the system up and running in minutes.
  • System Architecture: Deep dive into the modular monolith and tech stack.
  • API Reference: Explore the RESTful endpoints and streaming capabilities.
  • Development Workflow: Understand the engineering standards and quality gates.

docs.title: 🏛️ Project Vision
docs.text: The AI Audience Builder is designed to bridge the gap between natural language intent and deterministic advertising signals. By leveraging Gemini AI and a high-density Taxonomy Engine, it empowers planners to build precise, reachable audience segments through a conversational interface.

docs.title: 🛡️ Core Pillars
docs.text:
• Zero-Drift Execution: Perfect type synchronization across the monorepo boundary.
  • Principal-Grade Hygiene: Strict linting, type-safety, and automated testing.
  • AI Sovereignty: Controlled, manual validation of all AI-generated segments.
  • Observability: End-to-end request tracing and performance logging.

docs.title: 🏛️ System Architecture
docs.text: This document provides a high-level overview of the AI Audience Builder architecture, its core components, and the design principles that govern its development.

docs.title: 🌟 Core Philosophy
docs.text:
The AI Audience Builder is built on the principle of "Zero-Drift Engineering". Every architectural decision is made to ensure that the system remains type-safe, traceable, and highly maintainable as it scales.

  • Modular Monolith: The backend is structured as a collection of domain-specific modules, ensuring clear boundaries while maintaining the simplicity of a single deployment unit.
  • Contract-First: All data exchange between the frontend and backend is governed by a shared package of TypeScript interfaces.
  • State-as-URL: The frontend leverages the URL as the primary source of truth for the application state, enabling deep-linking and consistent user experiences.

docs.title: 🏗️ Project Structure
docs.text:
The project is organized as a Turborepo monorepo:

.
├── apps
│   ├── backend          # NestJS Modular Monolith
│   └── frontend         # React 19 + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4
├── packages
│   └── shared           # Shared DTOs, interfaces, and error keys
├── bruno                # API Collection for testing (Bruno)
├── docs                 # System & API Documentation
└── docker-compose.yml   # Container orchestration

docs.title: Backend (apps/backend)
docs.text:
• Framework: NestJS (Node.js)
  • Database: PostgreSQL (via Neon)
  • ORM: Prisma
  • AI Engine: Google Gemini AI
  • Caching: In-Memory (Standard)
  • Observability: Custom Correlation ID middleware & Performance Logging.

docs.title: Frontend (apps/frontend)
docs.text:
• Framework: React 19
  • Build Tool: Vite
  • Routing: React Router v7
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS v4

docs.title: 1. Identity & Auth (auth)
docs.text: Handles JWT-based authentication with Case-Insensitive Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) supporting ADMIN and PLANNER tiers.

docs.title: 2. Chat & AI Strategy (chat)
docs.text:
The core orchestration engine. It leverages Groq's high-performance inference to translate natural language prompts into a dual-part response:

  1. Conversational Reasoning: Natural language explanation of the targeting strategy.
  2. Structured Signals: A hidden JSON block containing validated taxonomy signals, reach estimates, and total audience counts.

This module utilizes Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time streaming to the frontend.

docs.title: 3. Taxonomy Engine (taxonomy)
docs.text: Manages the hierarchical targeting signals (Location, Transaction, Field Dictionaries). It provides the "Taxonomy Tree" that the AI uses to select specific segments.

docs.title: 4. Shared Contracts (@audience-builder/shared)
docs.text: Ensures that a change in the backend DTO is immediately reflected as a TypeScript error in the frontend, preventing runtime crashes.

docs.title: AI Guardrails
docs.text: The platform implements a "Planner-in-the-loop" model. AI-generated audience segments are recommendations that must be validated by a human Planner before being pushed to production targeting systems.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Every request is tagged with an x-correlation-id. This ID is propagated through logs, allowing developers to trace the lifecycle of a specific request from the frontend to the database.

docs.title: 🚀 Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide provides instructions for deploying the AI Audience Builder platform to production environments.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Summary for Deployment
docs.text:
• Backend: NestJS (deployed to Render)
  • Frontend: React/Vite (deployed to Vercel)
  • Database: PostgreSQL (Neon.tech recommended)
  • AI Engine: Groq (LLaMA 3.3 70B)

docs.title: 🛠️ Backend Deployment (Render)
docs.text: [!WARNING] Free Tier Cold Starts: Deploying to Render's Free Instance type means the service will spin down after 15 minutes of inactivity. The first request after a spin-down will experience a 30-50 second delay (Cold Start). For production workloads requiring instant response times, upgrade to a "Starter" instance.

docs.title: 1. New Web Service
docs.text:
Connect your GitHub repository and select the following settings:

  • Root Directory: (leave as project root)
  • Environment: Node
  • Build Command: pnpm install && pnpm run build --filter=@audience-builder/backend...
  • Start Command: pnpm --filter=@audience-builder/backend run start:prod

docs.title: 2. Backend Environment Variables
docs.text:
Add the following variables in the Render dashboard:

Variable Description DATABASE_URL Your PostgreSQL connection string (Neon.tech) JWT_SECRET A secure random string for signing tokens GROQ_API_KEY Your API key from Groq Console NODE_ENV production PORT 3000 (Render usually sets this automatically)

docs.title: 1. New Project
docs.text:
Connect your GitHub repository and select the following settings:

  • Framework Preset: Vite
  • Root Directory: (leave as project root)
  • Build Command: pnpm run build --filter=@audience-builder/frontend...
  • Output Directory: apps/frontend/dist

docs.title: 2. Frontend Environment Variables
docs.text:
Add the following variable:

Variable Value VITE_API_URL https://zerotoone-assignment.onrender.com/api/v1

docs.title: 🗄️ Database Initialization
docs.text:
Once the backend is deployed, you must seed the taxonomy data if you are using a fresh database:

# From your local machine, pointing to the PRODUCTION database URL in .env
pnpm db:seed

docs.title: 🔍 Post-Deployment Verification
docs.text:
1. Auth: Try logging in with the seeded credentials (admin@example.com / password123).
  2. AI Stream: Send a prompt like "Fitness enthusiasts in New York" and verify that the Groq stream completes and signal cards appear.
  3. Taxonomy: Navigate to the /taxonomy route and verify that the placeholder UI loads.
  4. Persistence: Refresh the page after a chat to ensure the conversation rehydrates from the database.

docs.title: 🛠️ Development Workflow
docs.text: This document outlines the engineering standards and workflows for contributing to the AI Audience Builder.

docs.title: 🤝 The Shared Contract Workflow
docs.text:
Because this is a monorepo with high type-safety requirements, you must follow the Shared Contract Workflow when modifying data structures.

  1. Modify the Contract: Update the interfaces in packages/shared/src/index.ts.
  2. Synchronize: Run pnpm build from the root. This ensures that the types are compiled and available to both apps/backend and apps/frontend.
  3. Implement: Update the backend service and then the frontend component.

[!WARNING] Do not define DTOs locally. If a data structure is used in an API request or response, it MUST reside in @audience-builder/shared.

docs.title: Modular Monolith Structure
docs.text:
Each feature should be encapsulated in a module under apps/backend/src/modules/.

  • *.module.ts: NestJS module definition.
  • *.controller.ts: API route handlers.
  • *.service.ts: Business logic (Keep controllers thin).
  • *.dto.ts: Local DTOs (only if they don't cross the network boundary).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: Use the shared ErrorKeys from the shared package to ensure the frontend can provide localized or user-friendly error messages.

docs.title: Design System
docs.text: We use Tailwind CSS v4. Avoid using ad-hoc CSS classes; stick to the design system tokens defined in index.css.

docs.title: State Management
docs.text:
• Local State: useState / useReducer for component-level UI state.
  • Global State: React Context for user sessions and global settings.
  • Persistent State: Use URL search parameters for filters, search queries, and selected items.

docs.title: 🧹 Hygiene & Quality Gates
docs.text:
This project enforces strict quality gates via Lefthook and git-hygiene.

  • Linting: All code must pass pnpm lint.
  • Formatting: Code must be formatted with Prettier via pnpm format.
  • Types: No any types allowed. Run pnpm check-types to verify workspace-wide type safety.

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
We follow Conventional Commits:

  • feat: New feature
  • fix: Bug fix
  • docs: Documentation changes
  • chore: Maintenance tasks

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Unit Tests: Place .spec.ts files alongside the source code. Focus on testing business logic in services.
  • Integration Tests: Focus on API endpoints and database interactions.
  • E2E Tests: Use the test:e2e command in the backend to verify the full request-response lifecycle.

docs.title: 🚀 CI/CD & Deployment
docs.text: We use GitHub Actions to automate our documentation deployment.

docs.title: 📖 Docs Pipeline (docs.yml)
docs.text: Automatically builds the MkDocs site and deploys it to GitHub Pages whenever changes are merged into the main branch.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will help you get your local development environment set up and running.

docs.title: 🛠️ Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Node.js: v24 or higher (LTS recommended)
  • pnpm: v10 or higher
  • Git: For version control
  • Docker: Optional (required for "Production Mirror" mode)

docs.title: 📥 Installation
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/chitrank2050/zerotoone-assignment.git
cd audience-builder
  1. Run the Setup Script: This project features a one-click bootstrap command that installs dependencies, generates Prisma clients, and applies database migrations.
pnpm run setup

docs.title: ⚙️ Environment Configuration
docs.text:
You must configure the environment variables for the backend to function correctly.

  1. Navigate to the backend directory:
cd apps/backend
  1. Create a .env file (you can copy .env.example if it exists):
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://user:password@neon-host.neon.tech/audience_builder?sslmode=require"
JWT_SECRET="your-high-entropy-secret"
GROQ_API_KEY="your-groq-console-api-key"
PORT=3000

docs.title: Local Development Mode
docs.text:
This mode provides the fastest feedback loop with Instant HMR (Hot Module Replacement).

# From the project root
pnpm dev
  • Frontend: http://localhost:5173
  • Backend API: http://localhost:3000

docs.title: Production Mirror Mode (Docker)
docs.text:
To verify how the application behaves in a containerized environment:

# Build and start containers
pnpm docker:build

# Stop containers
pnpm docker:down

docs.title: 🗄️ Database Management
docs.text:
We use PostgreSQL (Neon) and Prisma. For local development, you can either use a local PostgreSQL instance or a free tier project on Neon.tech.

[!TIP] Neon Setup: When using Neon, ensure your DATABASE_URL includes ?sslmode=require.

  • View Data: Use Prisma Studio to inspect your database visually.
cd apps/backend
pnpm dlx prisma studio
  • Seeding: To populate the database with initial taxonomy data:
pnpm run db:seed

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
Run the full test suite across the monorepo:

pnpm test

For interactive testing in watch mode:

pnpm test:watch

docs.title: 📖 Documentation
docs.text:
The project documentation is managed with MkDocs.

  • Live Site: https://chitrank2050.github.io/audience-builder/
  • Local Preview:
# Install mkdocs-material
pip install mkdocs-material

# Start local server
mkdocs serve

The documentation will be available at http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication API
docs.text: Endpoints for user authentication and session management.

docs.title: 🔑 Login
docs.text:
Authenticates a user and returns a JWT access token.

  • URL: /auth/login
  • Method: POST
  • Auth required: No

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
  "email": "planner@example.com",
  "password": "password123"
}

docs.text:
• Code: 200 OK
  • Content:
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1...",

docs.title: 💬 Chat & Conversations API
docs.text: Endpoints for interacting with the AI agent to build audience segments.

docs.title: 🧵 List Conversations
docs.text:
Retrieves all audience building sessions for the authenticated user.

  • URL: /chat/conversations
  • Method: GET
  • Auth required: Yes

docs.title: 📥 List Conversations Success Response
docs.text:
• Code: 200 OK
  • Content:

  "success": true,
  "data": [

docs.title: ✉️ Send Message
docs.text:
Sends a natural language prompt to the AI agent. The agent will respond with a text message and potentially a list of suggested taxonomy signals.

  • URL: /chat/messages
  • Method: POST
  • Auth required: Yes

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text:
{
  "conversationId": "conv_01", // Optional: ommit to start new conversation
  "content": "I want to target people in California who bought hiking gear recently."
}

docs.title: 📥 Send Message Success Response
docs.text:
• Code: 201 Created
  • Content:
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "msg_02",
    "role": "agent",
    "content": "I've analyzed your request. Based on our taxonomy, I recommend these segments...",
    "metadata": {
      "suggestedSignals": [
        { "id": "loc_ca", "name": "California", "type": "location" },
        {
          "id": "trans_hiking",
          "name": "Outdoor & Hiking",
          "type": "transaction"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 📖 Get Conversation History
docs.text:
Retrieves all messages for a specific conversation.

  • URL: /chat/conversations/:id
  • Method: GET
  • Auth required: Yes

docs.title: 📥 Get History Success Response
docs.text:
• Code: 200 OK
  • Content:
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "id": "conv_01",
    "messages": [
      { "role": "user", "content": "Hello" },
      {
        "role": "agent",
        "content": "How can I help you build an audience today?"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: ⚡ Stream AI Response (SSE)
docs.text:
Streams the AI response in real-time. Useful for "typing" effects in the UI.

  • URL: /chat/conversations/:id/stream
  • Method: GET
  • Auth required: Yes
  • Query Params: content (string) - The user's prompt.

docs.title: 📥 Stream Events
docs.text:
The endpoint returns a text/event-stream. Events are JSON-encoded.

Chunk Event:

{ "data": { "chunk": "I recommended " } }

Completion Event:

{ "data": { "done": true } }

Error Event:

{ "data": { "error": "Streaming failed" } }

docs.title: 🔌 API Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the AI Audience Builder API documentation. This API follows RESTful principles and returns JSON-encoded responses.

docs.title: 📍 Base URL
docs.text: • Development: http://localhost:3000

docs.title: 🔐 Authentication
docs.text:
Most endpoints require a JSON Web Token (JWT) provided in the Authorization header.

Authorization: Bearer <your_jwt_token>

Tokens are obtained via the /auth/login endpoint.

docs.title: 📦 Standard Response Format
docs.text:
All API responses follow a consistent wrapper format defined in @audience-builder/shared:

{
  "success": true,
  "data": { ... },
  "error": null,
  "metadata": {
    "requestId": "uuid-v4",
    "executionTime": "45ms"
  },
  "timestamp": "2024-05-12T10:00:00Z"
}
  • success: Boolean indicating if the request was successful.
  • data: The payload of the response (can be an object, array, or null).
  • error: A machine-readable error key if success is false.
  • metadata: Contextual information like correlation IDs and performance metrics.

docs.title: ⚠️ Error Handling
docs.text: Errors return a 4xx or 5xx HTTP status code and a JSON body containing an error key.

docs.title: Common Error Keys
docs.text: Key Description AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS Incorrect email or password. CHAT_CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND The requested conversation ID does not exist. TAXONOMY_INVALID_QUERY The search query for taxonomy signals is invalid. INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR An unexpected error occurred on the server.

Calculates the estimated reachable audience size for a combination of signals.

  • URL: /taxonomy/estimate
  • Method: POST
  • Auth required: Yes

  "signalIds": ["loc_01", "trans_hiking"]
